#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A stranger argument, put to all eighty-two tools (road map 7's D3·5, and
the gate of kpgalligan/framejob#21).

The startup parity check gained a FIFTH part with this ticket: every op tool's
declared arguments must be the core's own, every argument must carry a
description, and a description whose key is not an argument is a complaint
rather than a sentence dropped in silence. This script is the other half of
that, and the reason it exists is the series rule D3·3 and D3·4 both paid for:

> **A generated artefact is checked by asking the thing that generated it a
> question it did not write the answer to.**

The fifth part reads the same published table the catalog prints, so a
constraint the app still ENFORCES that the table stops DECLARING moves both
sides of its comparison together and passes. Twice in this series that
happened. So the weight here is on the sections that call the RUNNING TOOL and
read its answer: **for every op tool, every argument the tool calls required is
one the app refuses to do without, BY NAME** — which is a sentence written by
hand in fifty-eight handlers, against a required list that is now printed from
the core.

The sections, in order:

0. **The fifth part, made to complain.** A probe compiled from `app/Sources`
   builds the catalog this binary registers and puts it to
   `AgentServer.argumentFailure` — clean — and then puts four broken catalogs
   to it: an op tool with an argument the core has not got, one missing an
   argument the core has, one whose argument lost its description, and one
   whose prose names nothing. Each must be named with its op, its argument and
   the side that has it. An app-state tool broken the same way must draw
   NOTHING, which is the fourth part's skip rule.
1. **The catalog's size**, EXACTLY 90 PRODUCT tools — this script owns the
   exact count now and every older script keeps the floor the proof README's
   handover rule gives it — and the shipped binary's own parity log, which
   must be empty. The dev tools (road map 11, `dev_tools.py`) are counted
   apart: all present with the log's marker count equal to their number
   (Debug or Release), or all absent with no marker line (Distribution), and when
   present they sit together immediately before `import_media`, where
   `devTools()` splices them (V0's owed count and order probes).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Issue batch B44 — `close_project` and the held-path refusals (#40, spec
§11 #40), and `export_captions`' caption name rule (#43, spec §11 #43),
proved against the running app.

    python3 tools/proof/close_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]

`--log` defaults to `<dir>/framejob.log`. The app is a Release build
(the rows use the dev tools `snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item` and
`cancel_sheet`) at the socket, FRESH for each run: every row writes its own
package under `work/close_project/`, wiped at the start.

- **T1** — no `Frame Job: ` line in the log (the startup parity check).
- **K1** — `close_project` declares exactly `{discard, project}`: `discard`
  a boolean, nothing required.
- **C1** — 60 cycles of `new_project {path: c<NN>}` → `close_project
  {project: path}`, each answering that path (compared canonically) and
  `discarded_changes: false` — well past the ~40 open documents an instance
  deadlocks at when nothing closes one.
- **C2** — every `get_project {project: c<NN>}` is refused "No open project
  is at"; `snapshot_ui {}` lists no editor window for any of them; and
  `open_project c00` answers without `already_open` (then is closed).
- **C3** — the process's thread count after C1 is under its count before C1
  plus 64; both printed.
- **D1** — `new_project`, then the autosave guard; `close_project` is refused
  with the exact unsaved-changes sentence, and `get_project` still answers.
- **D2** — the autosave guard again on a second project, then
  `close_project {discard: true}` answers `discarded_changes: true`;
  `get_project` on it is refused, and its `project.json` on disk holds no
  marker at the last attempt's `at`.
- **H1** — a text clip on its own track, `save_project`, then
  `perform_menu_item ["File", "Export…"]` puts up a sheet and `close_project`
  is refused with the exact sheet sentence; after `cancel_sheet`,
  `close_project` answers.
- **S1** — with A and B open, `save_project {project: B, path: A}` and the
  same with `path: <dir>/./<A stem>` are both refused with the exact
  held-path sentence; B's path and A's `project.json` bytes are unchanged.
- **S2** — `new_project {path: A}` is refused with the exact sentence, and
  `snapshot_ui {}`'s editor-window count is unchanged.
- **S3** (control) — `save_project {project: A, path: A}` answers `saved`. It
  runs before S1, so a build that lets S1 write B over A cannot take it.
- **E1** — with a text clip on its own track, `export_captions {path:
  <work>/chart.png}` answers a `path` ending `/chart.png.srt`; that file
  exists and `chart.srt` does not.

**The autosave guard (D1, D2).** `ProjectDocument` autosaves in place, which
clears `unsaved_changes` some seconds after an edit. Each attempt adds a
marker at a fresh `at` (600000, 1200000, 1800000), reads `get_project`, and
calls `close_project` at once only if it answers `unsaved_changes: true`; on
`false` it prints `<ID> retry <n>: autosave landed` and tries again. Three
attempts at most; all three autosaved scores the row a failure.

**A wedged instance.** Every call waits at most 60 s. After the first call
that times out the script makes no more calls, and every row left scores
"fail — instance wedged at <row>".

Rows print as `<ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`. Exit 0 iff no row
failed.
"""

§11 #40), and `export_captions`' caption name rule (#43, spec §11 #43),
proved against the running app.

    python3 tools/proof/close_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]

`--log` defaults to `<dir>/framejob.log`. The app is a Release build
(the rows use the dev tools `snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item` and
`cancel_sheet`) at the socket, FRESH for each run: every row writes its own
package under `work/close_project/`, wiped at the start.

- **T1** — no `Frame Job: ` line in the log (the startup parity check).
- **K1** — `close_project` declares exactly `{discard, project}`: `discard`
  a boolean, nothing required.
- **C1** — 60 cycles of `new_project {path: c<NN>}` → `close_project
  {project: path}`, each answering that path (compared canonically) and
  `discarded_changes: false` — well past the ~40 open documents an instance
  deadlocks at when nothing closes one.
- **C2** — every `get_project {project: c<NN>}` is refused "No open project
  is at"; `snapshot_ui {}` lists no editor window for any of them; and
  `open_project c00` answers without `already_open` (then is closed).
- **C3** — the process's thread count after C1 is under its count before C1
  plus 64; both printed.
- **D1** — `new_project`, then the autosave guard; `close_project` is refused
  with the exact unsaved-changes sentence, and `get_project` still answers.
- **D2** — the autosave guard again on a second project, then
  `close_project {discard: true}` answers `discarded_changes: true`;
  `get_project` on it is refused, and its `project.json` on disk holds no
  marker at the last attempt's `at`.
- **H1** — a text clip on its own track, `save_project`, then
  `perform_menu_item ["File", "Export…"]` puts up a sheet and `close_project`
  is refused with the exact sheet sentence; after `cancel_sheet`,
  `close_project` answers.
- **S1** — with A and B open, `save_project {project: B, path: A}` and the
  same with `path: <dir>/./<A stem>` are both refused with the exact
  held-path sentence; B's path and A's `project.json` bytes are unchanged.
- **S2** — `new_project {path: A}` is refused with the exact sentence, and
  `snapshot_ui {}`'s editor-window count is unchanged.
- **S3** (control) — `save_project {project: A, path: A}` answers `saved`. It
  runs before S1, so a build that lets S1 write B over A cannot take it.
- **E1** — with a text clip on its own track, `export_captions {path:
  <work>/chart.png}` answers a `path` ending `/chart.png.srt`; that file
  exists and `chart.srt` does not.

**The autosave guard (D1, D2).** `ProjectDocument` autosaves in place, which
clears `unsaved_changes` some seconds after an edit. Each attempt adds a
marker at a fresh `at` (600000, 1200000, 1800000), reads `get_project`, and
calls `close_project` at once only if it answers `unsaved_changes: true`; on
`false` it prints `<ID> retry <n>: autosave landed` and tries again. Three
attempts at most; all three autosaved scores the row a failure.

**A wedged instance.** Every call waits at most 60 s. After the first call
that times out the script makes no more calls, and every row left scores
"fail — instance wedged at <row>".

Rows print as `<ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`. Exit 0 iff no row
failed.
"""

- **Content.** Three 8 s scenes at 1280×720, 30 fps (Dawn, Sea, Night), each with its own chord and drawn in the two OFL fonts already in `app/Resources/Fonts`. Each is placed as a 6 s clip with 1 s of spare footage at each end, back to back on Track 1 (0–18 s, no transition), with a 4,000,000-byte cap on the package.
- **Why the spare footage matters.** Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve calls `add_transition`, which is refused when neither clip has footage beyond the cut. The generator checks that the dissolve would apply at both cuts.
- **Media paths.** `project.json` stores placeholder paths that never resolve. On open, the existing `reanchoringConsolidatedMedia` repair points them at the package's own `media/` folder.
- **Opening it.** `PracticeProject.open()` copies the order of `untitled(around:)`: open an untitled document, set its name to "Practice Project", call `read(from:ofType:)` on the bundled package, then show the window. It does not touch `ProjectDocument.swift`, which is 1334 lines.
  - It deliberately avoids `duplicateDocument` and `init(for:withContentsOf:)`, which would make the app bundle the autosave location.
  - The copy opens clean; a save asks where, and the saved copy points at the media inside the app. TU-7 records this as an accepted risk: moving the app breaks those links until Relink or Consolidate Media.
- **Agent path.** `new_project` gains a `practice` argument rather than a new tool. A new tool would change the "one hundred and two tools" count in `CLAUDE.md`, the spec and the gate comment. `AgentCatalog.swift` must stay at or under 600 lines (it is 579 now).
- **Menu.** Help reads Frame Job Help, Tutorials ▸ (Open Practice Project), Graphics Reference, in a new `AppDelegate+Tutorials.swift`. TU3 will insert its per-page submenus above the item.
  - A failed open shows its error through `DispatchQueue.main.async { NSApp.presentError(error) }`. That keeps the menu item's verdict `window`, so `perform_menu_item` can drive it; the inventory's `reached_after` rule allows this, and `SaveFrame` is the precedent.
  - The item needs rows in `UIMenuTable.swift` and in `inventory.json`'s `selectors` and `sites`.
- **The `needs` check.** A new `app/Sources/TutorialClipFacts.swift` answers the filter's five keys for each clip, and TU2's runner can reuse it. The existing probe reads the bundled package through `PracticeProject.read`, the app's own open path, and prints each clip's facts and resolved media paths. `tutorial_check.py` then matches each tutorial's `needs.clip` by plain key equality, checks every media path is inside the package and checks `SHA256SUMS`. There is still one probe and no new `make test` line.
- **Spec §11.** TU-2 (3) gets definitions for `has_sound` and `has_pixels`, and a new TU-7 records the above. Both go in before any code.

**Other points:**
- **The four nits.** Each has a selftest case where it is a refusal: a refused tutorial comment now counts as one problem, `<!-- tutorial` inside a list item is refused, and a duplicate id is reported at line 7. The docstring fix needs no case. The selftest goes to 19 cases plus CONTROL (5 new; 3 cover the practice checks).
- **An existing probe needs editing.** `tools/proof/graphics_menu_probe.swift` checks that the Help menu is exactly `["Frame Job Help", "Graphics Reference"]` (line 120). The spec changes it and its proof's M3 docstring, and runs that proof in Full.
- **New MCP proof.** `tools/proof/practice_project_proof.py` covers both doors. It also confirms the bundled package is never written: its files match `SHA256SUMS` before and after edits and saves.
- **Verification.** Targeted runs the spec index proof, the selftest, the extractor under Python 3.9, `make typecheck`, `inventory.py --check`, `v2_menu.py --only H`, the generator, `tutorial_check.py`, and a Debug drive of the new proof. Full is `make gate`, then the practice and graphics-menu proofs against Release. Four mutants are listed.
- **Owed by the orchestrator.**
  - `CLAUDE.md` edits: root map rows for `tools/practice/` and `app/Resources/Practice/`, and the `make test` line's `tutorial_check.py` clause.
  - `app/CLAUDE.md` entries: `TutorialClipFacts.swift`, `PracticeProject.swift`, and `+Tutorials` in the AppDelegate family line.
- **Owner choice.** The scenes' look and sound are built as the spec describes, and the owner judges them in the new manual check TUT-1.
